doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Harry Allen and humor among musicians
summary: Praise for young tenor Harry Allen, and the role of humor in jazz.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Are there any other musicians that you played with that you shared a particularly fun or fulfilling experience with?

Well there’s a new guy that I have worked with that I find is just a delightful guy to play with and he’s only 27 years old and he’s also my tennis — he’s the guy that ruined my wrist. We played tennis together. He lives right across the river. I live right in Manhattan and he lives right across the river and I get in my car and drive over and play tennis with him whenever I can. And his name is Harry Allen. You ever heard of him by any chance?

Well he started out, now I met him when he was sixteen. Scott Hamilton used to let him sit in because he liked his playing and he loved Scott Hamilton. But now he’s developed into, he’s going to really be a — you’re going to hear a lot about this guy Harry Allen. He doesn’t play, he’s a swing tenor man. Plus he’s a delightful guy, you know, really a joy to play with, just a lot of fun, a lot of laughs, jokes all the time. So that’s nice.
Humor is a big part of this music, isn’t it?

Yeah. That’s what my wife tells me. She says the funniest that I am is when I’m around musicians that I guess, when they get together somehow it just comes out, the humor somehow. I don’t understand why, what it is. But if you’re around it, well you seem to know a lot about that. I observed it myself. It’s just jokes and so forth, a lot of jokes.
